title: Programming Concepts & OOP
description: Interactive Revision Cheat Sheet & Interview Guide

topics.title: VARIABLES, REFERENCES & POINTERS
topics.explanation:
Variable is a named storage location used to store data that can be accessed and modified during program execution. There are 2 types of Variables: 
 ->Primitive types generally store the actual value directly. 
->Reference types represent or refer to objects stored elsewhere in memory. 
 Pointer: pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable.
topics.tldr: Variable হলো data রাখার জন্য নাম দেওয়া একটি memory location। Pointer variable-এর value না, তার memory address ধরে রাখে।
keyPoints: Primitive types store the actual value directly (e.g., int, char, float, double, bool).
Reference types represent or refer to objects stored elsewhere in memory (e.g., Objects, Arrays, Classes, Strings in many languages).
The exact memory size of data types depends on the programming language, compiler, and platform. Avoid memorizing sizes as universal facts.
Address: The memory location of a variable.
Dereferencing: Accessing the value stored at the memory address held by a pointer.
Pointer to Pointer: A pointer that stores the address of another pointer.

codeSnippets.explanation: Example of pointer and dereferencing in C++.

comparisons.title: Important C++ Operators
rows: Gets the memory address of a variable
Dereferences a pointer to access the value

traps.statement: Does every variable directly store the actual data?
traps.explanation: No. Value types typically store the value directly, while reference types store or use a reference to access an object.

traps.statement: What happens if you dereference a null or invalid pointer?
traps.explanation: It results in undefined behavior and may crash the program. Never dereference an uninitialized pointer or nullptr.

topics.title: JAVASCRIPT VALUE VS REFERENCE
topics.explanation: In JavaScript, primitive values (like numbers, strings, booleans) are copied by value, meaning each variable holds its own copy of the data. Objects (including arrays and functions) are copied by reference, meaning multiple variables can refer to the same object in memory.
topics.tldr: Primitive copy করলে আলাদা value হয়, কিন্তু Object assign করলে সাধারণত একই object-এর reference share হয়।

traps.statement: const prevents object mutation
traps.explanation: const prevents reassignment of the variable. It does not automatically make the object immutable. `user.name = "Alice";` is valid, but `user = {};` throws an error.

traps.statement: How can you create a shallow copy of an object?
traps.explanation: Use the spread syntax: `const userCopy = { ...user };` or `const copy = [...array];`. Important: Spread syntax creates a shallow copy. Nested objects may still share references.

topics.title: PASS BY VALUE VS PASS BY REFERENCE
topics.explanation: Pass by value gives a function a copy of the argument, while pass by reference allows a function to access the original object or variable through a reference mechanism.
topics.tldr: Pass by value-তে copy যায়, pass by reference-এ original data modify করা সম্ভব।

comparisons.title: Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference
rows: A copy of the value is passed
Reference or alias to the original is passed
Changes usually do not affect the original variable
Changes can affect the original variable

questions.question: What is the difference between pass by value and pass by reference?
questions.answer: Pass by value passes a copy, while pass by reference allows the function to operate on the original variable through a reference.

topics.title: C++ POINTERS & MEMORY
topics.explanation: Arrays store elements sequentially in memory, enabling pointer arithmetic access.
topics.tldr: Array-এর elementগুলো sequential memory-তে থাকে, তাই pointer দিয়ে next element access করা যায়।

traps.statement: Is pointer arithmetic safe everywhere?
traps.explanation: No. Pointer arithmetic should remain within the bounds of the same array or valid memory region.

topics.title: STACK VS HEAP MEMORY
topics.explanation: Stack and heap are two important areas of memory commonly discussed in programming interviews. Stack memory is typically associated with function calls and local variables, while heap memory is commonly used for dynamically allocated objects and data.
topics.tldr: Stack সাধারণত function call ও local data-এর জন্য, Heap সাধারণত dynamically allocated data-এর জন্য ব্যবহৃত হয়।

comparisons.title: Stack vs Heap
rows: Managed manually or by garbage collection depending on language

questions.question: What is the difference between stack and heap memory?
questions.answer: Stack memory is primarily used for function-call frames and local data, while heap memory is used for dynamically allocated data and objects.

questions.question: Why can stack overflow happen?
questions.answer: It can happen when the call stack grows beyond its available limit, commonly because of excessive recursion or deeply nested function calls.

traps.statement: All objects are always stored entirely on the heap.
traps.explanation: This is language- and implementation-dependent. Avoid treating simplified memory models as universal rules.

topics.title: MUTABLE VS IMMUTABLE
topics.explanation: A mutable object can be changed after creation, while an immutable value or object cannot be changed directly after creation.
topics.tldr: Mutable data change করা যায়, immutable data directly change করা যায় না।

comparisons.title: Mutable vs Immutable
rows: Cannot be directly modified after creation
Changes generally require creating a new value

questions.question: Why is immutability useful?
questions.answer: Immutable values are easier to reason about and can reduce unexpected side effects when data is shared.

questions.question: Is const the same as immutable in JavaScript?
questions.answer: No. const prevents reassignment of the variable, but an object referenced by const can still be mutated.

topics.title: SHALLOW COPY VS DEEP COPY
topics.explanation: A shallow copy creates a new outer object while nested objects may still share references. A deep copy creates independent copies of nested data.
topics.tldr: Shallow copy-তে nested reference share হতে পারে, Deep copy-তে nested data-ও আলাদা হয়।

codeSnippets.explanation: Spread syntax creates a shallow copy.
structuredClone creates a deep copy for supported values.

questions.question: What is the difference between shallow copy and deep copy?
questions.answer: A shallow copy may share nested references, while a deep copy creates independent copies of nested data.

topics.title: PRE-INCREMENT VS POST-INCREMENT
topics.explanation:
Post-Increment (x++): Use the current value first, then increment.
Pre-Increment (++x): Increment first, then use the updated value.
topics.tldr: x++ আগে use পরে বাড়ে, ++x আগে বাড়ে পরে use হয়।

questions.question: Are x++ and ++x always interchangeable?
questions.answer: No. They produce different results when the expression's value is used.

topics.title: FUNCTIONS, PARAMETERS & ARGUMENTS
topics.explanation: A function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task. Parameters are variables defined by the function, while arguments are the actual values supplied when calling it.
topics.tldr: Parameter function definition-এ থাকে, argument function call-এর সময় দেওয়া actual value।

questions.question: What is a function?
questions.answer: A reusable block of code designed to perform a specific task.

questions.question: What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?
questions.answer: A parameter is defined in a function declaration, while an argument is the actual value passed during a function call.

topics.title: CONTROL FLOW & LOOPS
topics.explanation: Different types of loops serve different purposes based on whether the number of iterations is known and when the condition is checked.
topics.tldr: do...while condition false হলেও অন্তত একবার execute হবেই।

codeSnippets.explanation: Use when the number of iterations is known.
Use when the number of iterations is unknown.
Runs the code block before checking the condition. The loop runs once even though the condition is false (Output: 10).

questions.question: Which loop guarantees at least one execution?
questions.answer: do...while.

topics.title: COMMON STRING & ARRAY OPERATIONS
topics.explanation: Essential Operations: Length, Character Access, Uppercase, Lowercase, Find, Search, Contains, Substring, Replace, Split, Join, Trim, Concatenate, Compare, Repeat.
topics.tldr: Built-in function use করার আগে complexity আর original data change হয় কিনা দেখে নাও।

comparisons.title: Common String Operations
rows: Returns -1, false, or an error if the item is missing

traps.statement: Is every built-in operation O(1)?
traps.explanation: No. Searching, copying, replacing, sorting, and creating substrings may require O(n) or more operations.

topics.title: COMMON COLLECTION DATA STRUCTURES
topics.explanation: Comparison of List, Set, and Tuple-like collection data structures across programming languages.
topics.tldr: List সাধারণত ordered ও mutable collection, Set unique elements রাখে, আর Tuple সাধারণত ordered ও immutable collection হিসেবে ব্যবহৃত হয়। Exact behavior language অনুযায়ী ভিন্ন হতে পারে।

comparisons.title: List, Set & Tuple Comparison
rows: Fixed or immutable collection of elements

questions.question: Why are sets useful in algorithms?
questions.answer: Sets provide efficient average-case membership checking in many languages and are useful for duplicate detection and lookup problems.

topics.title: CALLBACK FUNCTIONS & forEach()
topics.explanation:
A callback function is a function passed as an argument to another function and executed by that function. 
`forEach()` executes a callback function once for each element of an array.
topics.tldr: forEach() দিয়ে loop করা সহজ, কিন্তু মাঝপথে break করা যায় না।

traps.statement: You can use break or continue inside forEach().
traps.explanation: You generally cannot use break or continue inside a normal forEach() callback. If you need early termination, consider: for, for...of, .some(), .every(), .find().

questions.question: What is the difference between forEach() and map()?
questions.answer: forEach() is mainly used for side effects. map() transforms elements and returns a new array.

topics.title: HIGHER-ORDER FUNCTIONS & ARRAY METHODS
topics.explanation: A higher-order function accepts another function as an argument, returns a function, or both. JavaScript array methods such as map, filter, reduce, find, some, and every commonly use callbacks.
topics.tldr: Callback function হলো অন্য function-এ argument হিসেবে দেওয়া function; Higher-order function হলো যে function অন্য function গ্রহণ করে বা return করে।

comparisons.title: Common JavaScript Array Methods
rows: Perform an action for each element
Check whether at least one matches

questions.question: What is a higher-order function?
questions.answer: A function that accepts another function as an argument, returns a function, or both.

questions.question: What is the difference between map() and filter()?
questions.answer: map() transforms every element and returns a new array, while filter() returns a new array containing only elements that satisfy a condition.

questions.question: What is the difference between find() and filter()?
questions.answer: find() returns the first matching element, while filter() returns all matching elements in a new array.

topics.title: RECURSION
topics.explanation: Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller versions of the same problem. Every recursive solution requires a Base Case and a Recursive Case.
topics.tldr: Function নিজেকে ছোট problem নিয়ে বারবার call করে, Base Case এ গিয়ে থামে।

traps.statement: What happens if recursion has no base case?
traps.explanation: The function may continue calling itself until the call stack limit is exceeded, causing a stack overflow or recursion error.

topics.title: TIME COMPLEXITY
topics.explanation: Time Complexity describes how the number of operations performed by an algorithm grows as the input size n increases. It does not measure actual execution time in seconds.
topics.tldr: Input বাড়লে algorithm-এর কাজ কত দ্রুত বাড়ে, সেটাই Time Complexity।

codeSnippets.explanation: Example: O(n) - The loop runs n times.
Example: O(n²) - Time Complexity is quadratic.

traps.statement: Do two loops always mean O(n²)?
traps.explanation: No. Consecutive loops result in O(n) + O(n) = O(2n) = O(n). Nested loops may produce O(n²).

topics.title: SPACE COMPLEXITY
topics.explanation: Space Complexity measures how an algorithm's memory usage grows as input size increases.
topics.tldr: Input বাড়লে algorithm-এর extra memory কত বাড়ে, সেটাই Space Complexity।

codeSnippets.code: vector<int> result(n);
codeSnippets.explanation: Example with Extra Array. Extra space: O(n)

questions.question: Does input memory always count as extra space?
questions.answer: Usually, interviewers distinguish between input space and auxiliary space. Always clarify whether you are discussing total space or extra space used by the algorithm.

topics.title: OBJECT-ORIENTED PROGRAMMING CONCEPTS
topics.explanation:
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm that organizes software around objects. An object combines data (attributes) and behavior (methods).
The four pillars are: Encapsulation, Inheritance, Abstraction, Polymorphism.
topics.tldr: Class হলো blueprint, Object হলো blueprint থেকে তৈরি real instance। Procedural-এ function main, OOP-তে object main।

codeSnippets.explanation: Class and Object example. Car is the class, myCar is the object.
Constructor Overloading: Default and Parameterized Constructors.

traps.statement: Does a class always consume no memory?
traps.explanation: That statement is oversimplified. Objects consume memory for instance data. Static members and implementation details may also require memory.

traps.statement: Can a constructor have a return type?
traps.explanation: No. A constructor does not have a return type, including void.

traps.statement: Is encapsulation simply making every variable private?
traps.explanation: No. The main goal is to control access and protect the object's valid state. Getters and setters should provide meaningful control when necessary.

traps.statement: What problem can multiple inheritance cause?
traps.explanation: It can cause ambiguity, including the Diamond Problem. C++ can handle this using techniques such as virtual inheritance.

topics.title: CONSTRUCTOR & DESTRUCTOR
topics.explanation: A constructor initializes an object when it is created. A destructor performs cleanup when an object is destroyed in languages such as C++ that provide deterministic object destruction.
topics.tldr: Constructor object তৈরি হওয়ার সময় initialize করে; Destructor object destroy হওয়ার সময় cleanup করে।

comparisons.title: Constructor vs Destructor
rows: Called when object lifetime ends in C++
Has the same name as the class

questions.question: Can a constructor have a return type?
questions.answer: No. A constructor does not have a return type, including void.

questions.question: Can a destructor be overloaded?
questions.answer: No. A class can have only one destructor.

questions.question: What is a copy constructor?
questions.answer: A constructor that creates an object from another object of the same class, commonly used to copy its state.

topics.title: ACCESS MODIFIERS
topics.explanation: Access modifiers control where class members can be accessed. Common C++ access modifiers are public, private, and protected.
topics.tldr: public everywhere accessible, private class-এর ভিতরে controlled access, protected class ও derived class-এর জন্য accessible।

comparisons.title: C++ Access Modifiers
rows: Accessible within the class and derived classes

questions.question: What is the purpose of access modifiers?
questions.answer: They control access to class members and help enforce encapsulation.

topics.title: VIRTUAL FUNCTIONS & DYNAMIC BINDING
topics.explanation: A virtual function allows a derived class implementation to be selected through a base-class pointer or reference at runtime. This enables runtime polymorphism in C++.
topics.tldr: virtual function runtime-এ actual object-এর overridden method select করতে সাহায্য করে।

codeSnippets.explanation: Runtime dispatch through a virtual function.

questions.question: Why is the virtual keyword used in C++?
questions.answer: It enables dynamic dispatch so an overridden derived-class method can be selected at runtime through a base-class pointer or reference.

questions.question: What is dynamic binding?
questions.answer: Dynamic binding means the method implementation to execute is determined at runtime based on the actual object type.

topics.title: ABSTRACT CLASS VS INTERFACE
topics.explanation: An abstract class defines a common abstraction and may contain both implemented and abstract behavior. An interface primarily defines a contract that implementing classes must satisfy; the exact implementation depends on the programming language.
topics.tldr: Abstract class shared implementation রাখতে পারে; Interface মূলত behavior-এর contract define করে।

comparisons.title: Abstract Class vs Interface
rows: Can contain state depending on language

questions.question: What is an abstract class?
questions.answer: A class intended to serve as a base abstraction and generally cannot be instantiated directly when it contains abstract operations.

questions.question: What is an interface?
questions.answer: An interface defines a contract of behavior that implementing classes must provide; exact syntax and capabilities depend on the language.

topics.title: ERROR & EXCEPTION HANDLING
topics.explanation: Error handling allows a program to detect, handle, or propagate abnormal situations instead of failing unexpectedly. Exception mechanisms vary between programming languages.
topics.tldr: Exception handling unexpected runtime situations safely handle বা propagate করতে সাহায্য করে।

comparisons.title: Common Exception Handling Concepts
rows: Contains code that may produce an exception
Runs cleanup code in languages that support it

questions.question: Why is exception handling important?
questions.answer: It allows programs to handle abnormal situations gracefully and separate error-handling logic from normal program flow.

questions.question: What is the purpose of try-catch?
questions.answer: try contains potentially failing code, while catch handles an exception raised from that code.

topics.title: LIBRARY VS NAMESPACE
topics.explanation:
Library is a collection of reusable code such as functions, classes, utilities, and modules. 
Namespace creates a logical scope to organize names and avoid naming conflicts.
topics.tldr: Library feature দেয়, Namespace name conflict আটকায়।

questions.question: Does a namespace itself provide functionality?
questions.answer: No. A namespace organizes identifiers. The functions and classes inside it provide the actual functionality.

topics.title: COMMON PROGRAMMING PITFALLS
topics.explanation: Programming interviews often test awareness of common mistakes involving memory, references, loops, object state, and function behavior.
topics.tldr: Interview-এ শুধু syntax না, common bugs এবং edge cases চিনতে পারাও important।
keyPoints: Null or invalid pointer dereferencing can cause undefined behavior.
Infinite loops can occur when loop conditions never become false.
Stack overflow can occur because of excessive recursion or deeply nested calls.
Shared object references can cause unexpected mutations.
Using a shallow copy does not necessarily isolate nested objects.
Incorrect boundary conditions can cause off-by-one errors.
Resource management should be handled appropriately for the language and runtime.

questions.question: What is an off-by-one error?
questions.answer: An off-by-one error occurs when a loop or index boundary is one position too high or too low.

questions.question: What is an infinite loop?
questions.answer: A loop that never reaches its termination condition and continues executing indefinitely.

topics.title: COMMON INTERVIEW QUESTIONS
topics.explanation: Frequently asked interview questions covering core OOP concepts and logic.

questions.question: Q1. What is the difference between a Class and an Object?
questions.answer: A class is a blueprint that defines properties and behavior. An object is an instance created from that class and contains actual runtime state.

questions.question: Q2. What is a Constructor?
questions.answer: A constructor is a special member function that automatically executes when an object is created. It initializes the object's state and performs setup.

questions.question: Q3. What is the difference between Overloading and Overriding?
questions.answer: Overloading uses the same function name with different parameter lists and is generally resolved at compile time. Overriding occurs when a derived class provides its own implementation of an inherited method and supports runtime polymorphism.

questions.question: Q4. Why do we use Getters and Setters?
questions.answer: Getters and setters provide controlled access to object data. They allow: Validation, Data protection, Controlled modification, Better maintainability.

questions.question: Q5. What are the Four Pillars of OOP?
questions.answer: Encapsulation, Inheritance, Abstraction, Polymorphism.

questions.question: Q6. What is the difference between Abstraction and Encapsulation?
questions.answer: Abstraction hides unnecessary implementation details and exposes essential functionality. Encapsulation controls access to data and groups data with related methods.

questions.question: Q7. What is Runtime Polymorphism?
questions.answer: Runtime polymorphism occurs when the method to execute is determined during program execution based on the object's actual runtime type. In C++, it is commonly achieved using: virtual, Method overriding, Base class pointers or references.

questions.question: Q8. What is the difference between Stack and Heap?
questions.answer: Stack memory is primarily associated with function calls and local data, while heap memory is commonly used for dynamically allocated data and objects.

questions.question: Q9. What is Pass by Value vs Pass by Reference?
questions.answer: Pass by value passes a copy, while pass by reference allows access to the original variable through a reference mechanism.

questions.question: Q10. What is Shallow Copy vs Deep Copy?
questions.answer: A shallow copy may share nested references, while a deep copy creates independent copies of nested data.

questions.question: Q11. What is the difference between map() and filter()?
questions.answer: map() transforms every element and returns a new array, while filter() returns elements that satisfy a condition.

questions.question: Q12. What is a Higher-Order Function?
questions.answer: A function that accepts another function as an argument, returns a function, or both.

questions.question: Q13. What is a Virtual Function?
questions.answer: A virtual function enables runtime method dispatch through a base-class pointer or reference in C++.

questions.question: Q14. What is an Abstract Class?
questions.answer: An abstract class provides a base abstraction and generally cannot be instantiated directly when it contains abstract operations.

questions.question: Q15. What is Exception Handling?
questions.answer: Exception handling is a mechanism for detecting and handling abnormal situations without allowing the program to fail unexpectedly.

flashcards.question: What is a Pointer?

flashcards.question: What is a Reference Type?

flashcards.question: What is Time Complexity?
flashcards.answer: A measure of how the number of operations grows as input size increases.

flashcards.question: What is Space Complexity?

flashcards.question: What is a Class?

flashcards.question: What is an Object?

flashcards.question: What is Inheritance?

flashcards.question: What is Immutable?
flashcards.answer: Data that cannot be directly modified after creation.

flashcards.question: What is Deep Copy?
flashcards.answer: A copy where nested data is independently copied.

flashcards.question: What is a Higher-Order Function?
flashcards.answer: A function that accepts or returns another function.

flashcards.answer: A mechanism for handling abnormal program situations.

topics.title: FINAL INTERVIEW TRAP CHECKLIST & STRATEGY
topics.explanation: A checklist of common interview traps and an answering strategy using a One-Line Memory Map.
keyPoints: For most Computer Science interview questions, use this structure: 1. Definition 2. Key Mechanism 3. Example 4. Edge Case or Difference.

traps.statement: "Nested loops always mean O(n²)."
traps.explanation: Consecutive loops can still be O(n).

traps.statement: "const makes JavaScript objects immutable."
traps.explanation: const prevents reassignment but object properties may still change.

traps.statement: "A class never uses memory."
traps.explanation: This statement is oversimplified. Objects clearly occupy memory, and static members or implementation details may also require memory.

traps.statement: "Primitive types always have the same size."
traps.explanation: Memory size can depend on language, compiler, architecture, and platform.

traps.statement: "forEach() supports break."
traps.explanation: Use for, for...of, .some(), or .find() when early termination is needed.

traps.statement: "Recursion only needs a recursive call."
traps.explanation: Recursion must have a proper base case.

traps.statement: "Overloading and Overriding are the same."
traps.explanation: Overloading is based on different parameters. Overriding replaces inherited behavior in a derived class.

traps.statement: "Making all variables private automatically means good encapsulation."
traps.explanation: Good encapsulation means meaningful control over access and object state.

traps.statement: "Pass by value always means the original object can never be affected."
traps.explanation: The exact behavior depends on the language and the value being passed. In JavaScript, an object reference itself is passed by value, so object mutation can affect the original object.

traps.statement: "Shallow copy always creates a completely independent object."
traps.explanation: No. Nested objects can still share references after a shallow copy.

traps.statement: "Stack and heap behavior is identical in every programming language."
traps.explanation: No. Memory management and object placement are language- and implementation-dependent.

traps.statement: "A higher-order function is the same thing as a callback."
traps.explanation: A callback is a function passed to another function, while a higher-order function is a function that accepts or returns functions. A callback is often used with a higher-order function.
